parts.description: A solid light gray ceramic coffee mug with a cylindrical body and a curved side handle. The object features a smooth, lightly glazed finish and a subtle stepped base.
parts.reasoning: The object is visually identifiable as a standard ceramic or stoneware coffee mug. Given typical dimensions for this form factor (approximately 9-10 cm in height and 8 cm in diameter) and a standard wall thickness, the volume of the material is estimated to yield a mass of roughly 0.35 kg. The density is set to 2400 kg/m³, which is representative of dense, fired ceramics. For friction, glazed ceramic is relatively smooth, so static and dynamic friction coefficients are set to moderate-to-low values (0.4 and 0.35, respectively). Ceramic is a rigid, brittle material that absorbs impact energy rather than bouncing, justifying a low restitution value of 0.2. For Isaac Sim simulation, a 'convex_decomposition' collider type is strictly necessary to accurately represent both the hollow inner cavity of the cup and the opening of the handle; a standard convex hull would incorrectly close these gaps.
